frequency_question: How often do central banks execute a planned liquidity-absorbing structural tool when liquidity conditions warrant and authority is undisputed?
membership_rule: Members are defined as policy actions by major central banks (RBI, PBoC, Bank Indonesia, etc.) introducing a non-standard, targeted reserve ratio or liquidity-freezing instrument within a defined tightening cycle. Excluded are standard rate changes and open market operations.

cases.name: PBoC targeted reserve requirement ratio (RRR) adjustments
Bank Indonesia secondary reserve requirement adjustment
PBoC central bank bills issuance for targeted sterilization

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 named major emerging market episodes; believed representative of all clear-cut cases where the central bank possessed unconstrained statutory authority.
known_gaps: Excludes minor adjustments by smaller tier-2 central banks.
skeleton: Total major central bank targeted liquidity-instrument deployments executed upon identification of excess liquidity during structural tightening phases.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 documented major emerging market liquidity-instrument deployment episodes where the mandate and intent were explicitly declared.
validity_reason: Central bank statutory powers regarding reserve ratios and liquidity management instruments remain stable over multi-decade horizons.
